10:29 as someone who crochets and knits, I’d say a lot of that is genuinely doable, but would cost hundreds, maybe even thousands because of the amount of work it would take to make one. The dragon face would have a lot more texture, and there would need to be wires and a lot of sewing…plus a lot of that jumper texture is just random lines because AI just smashes hundreds of thousands of images together of all different stitch and yarn types so that would be different, but I’d say it would be doable.

It would also be very heavy and uncomfortable on your back because of the amount of weight and stitching that would go into the back section. Amigurumi gets pretty heavy when you incorporate wiring and parts to keep its shape, and it would make it very difficult to wash, wear with any form of backpack, sit down on a backed chair with, all sorts of different things. It’s one of those things where you go “oh that’s cool” until you or someone who knows what they’re doing sits down to actually make it and you realise that yarn doesn’t just sit right where you put it without stitching and stuffing, and that you don’t really want sticking out parts or possibly sharp wires on the back of your jumpers. 

Also just designing something like this would be a nightmare. It’s one thing to put an image using different colours (tapestry knitting, embroidery, that type of thing), but to create a seamless jumper with a face popping out of the back and a braid coming down and around…creating the pattern and figuring out dimensions for all that alone could take days, and finding different yarn gauges for all the details in the same colour combinations would be hell unless you self dye (which can also be hell). That jumper would probably weigh around 2Kg also, with the amount of material needed, which is 20 BALLS OF NORMAL SIZED YARN. Even on good days that’s at least £100, or $120-130, probably half that on wholesale but anyone planning to do this type of thing usually either does one off commissions or it’s an art piece, so it’s not usually bought wholesale for those types of projects.

Don’t fall for the scams, it breaks my heart seeing all these and then people believing genuine art pieces are therefore AI because they couldn’t conceive them. If you want something like this, look for a well known commission artist that does this, get a quote, and if you can afford it, get a piece of work done that will last and you can enjoy for a long time because of its quality and love and care. They probably can’t make something day to day wearable of this nature, but they know a lot about custom pieces usually and can probably create something that would be far more comfortable, manageable, and dare I say cooler because it was envisioned by a human being.

since you mentioned the absurd shark fiend & chainsaw man sequence which coincidentally is an actual reference to SHARNADO. the author is a huge movie buff so here are some references & interesting quips from the movie :

during the opening song, there are references to CONSTANTINE, Bande a' part (THE BAND OF OUTSIDERS) & the very first motion picture of a man riding a horse

during the makima movie marathon date sequence, you can hear sound bites from TEXAS CHAINSAW MASSACRE & PSYCHO. the movie that makes them shed some tear is a real soviet era film from 1959 called BALLAD OF A SOLDIER. makes sense since Reze is from Soviet Union

on the rooftop, the choking action that takes place references Anton Chigur choking out the sheriff in NO COUNTRY FOR OLD MEN. also, Reze sings that song in original russian hinting at her soviet roots as a trained KGB type assassin

the Bomb devil design itself, especially the nuke-type head is referencing the Xenomorph from ALIEN. Public safety's uniform itself is a reference to the outfits from RESERVOIR DOGS, all suited up in black

Denji & Beam enact the famous NAPOLEON CROSSING THE ALPS painting 🤣. the manga-esque splash page animation when they defeat the typhoon devil is referencing a very infamous manga panel from BERSERK (Guts riding Zodd)

As someone who's been a pretty diehard anime fan since I was 11 (now 26) I can tell you that when an anime doesn't have much animation, it's ALWAYS because of a lack of time and animators. There are obviously some animators and directors who stand out, but less acclaimed animators do a great job if they're just given an appropriate amount of time. The reason why things like this happen is because of production committees, not anime studios. The production committees decide pretty much everything and the studio just has to work within the constraints they're given. If a production committee tells JC Staff that they have to release a new OPM season by (x) date, then they have to do it regardless of how much time or money is invested into it. There was a very similar controversy when Blue Lock season 2 aired, and it came out that many of the early episodes were animated in large part by just one guy. And this is the type of stuff that happens when production committees give unreasonable demands to anime studios.

If you really like One Punch Man I highly recommend Mob Psycho 100! ONE is the author of both series, so they have similar art styles and brands of humor. Mob is completed with three seasons, and the animation is beautiful throughout the show. It's like if OPM kept its quality from season one.

Buyer beware of the dirty secrets of wine producers.  Besides some chemicals, other additives can find their way into a bottle of wine for the manufacturer to keep a standard mouthfeel, color and flavor profile. Food coloring, commercial yeast, sugar and acidifiers are some of those extra ingredients that help give consumers exactly what they are expecting from a specific brand. Some of those names include gum arabic, activated carbon, ammonium phosphate, alumino-silicates, ascorbic acid, citric acid, copper sulfate, polyoxythylene 40, dimethyl dicarbonate, carbohydrase, oak chips, tannin and, my personal favorite, the mysterious mega purple. But why don't I see "mega purple" or "polyoxythylene 40" listed anywhere on my wine bottle? The reason is because there are no rules for labeling wine. The game feels short from the lack of content like drawn out boss battles and world building

They didn’t give us enough foreshadowing like the other games. They should have progressed alone’s sickness or they should have progressively damaged the mirror to have the players predict something else is going on

The mechanics that were introduced weren’t prevalent to the rest of the game like when mono has his warp as an ability than low using his mirror at the end of each chapter they could have extended to that

The game is pricey for the available content where they are introducing 2 dlc’s that are apart of the game.

The overall visuals weren’t as appealing to their counterparts as they are repetitive and dull and they didn’t bring significance.  

The ending felt like a cliffhanger even with the secret ending, it could be interpreted differently than what little nightmares usually had which were long drawn out cinematic endings, it was short and brisk right after the final boss.

You already mentioned something similar but I think there was only 1 peacemaker helmet used in the whole season (magic stars, which was great). The other action scene was good, but the whole 'Sons of Liberty actually being the anti-nazis' is only brought up when the 2 vigilantes meet and Chris never has to reckon with the fact that the people he killed were the good guys.

Speaking of Adrian, he was criminally underused this season. Only really used as one of many comic relief characters when there was a huge and obvious opportunity for multiple arcs/moments with him and Chris.

1) There could have been a buildup of Chris wanting to be like a big brother to Adrian over the course of the season and trying to rein him in to go through the growth Chris went through in season 1. It would make Chris hanging around with Adrian make more sense (outside of the one gun comedy scene in season 1 their relationship has seemed completely one sided), and it would have made the whole choosing between the two worlds and 'your true family is the one you've made back in your home world' hit harder. Also tying in with above, Chris choosing the other world would've seemed more like a betrayal to Adrian than it really did.

2) Adrian kills alt world Chris's dad without knowing he's not a nazi (although I felt like that twist kind of came out of nowhere) and almost kills his brother. Why does him being the sole cause of his best friend having a mental breakdown not affect him in any way? I get that he's supposed to be an insane psychopath kind of character but I feel like Freddie Stroma was really good and giving him another angle of the character by having Adrian actually take something seriously for once would've been nice.

Another crazy decision is that whole nazi world is just forgotten about in the finale. Like I thought the closeup on Keith was implying a showdown next episode, and it would make sense since the nazi world just lost two (almost all 3) of their 'Top Trio'.

It would literally be so easy too. Unless I'm forgetting something from earlier, they could just say that the alien tech will fit any doorway (like a hangar or warehouse door or something) and use that to allow for many people to pass through at once. They already hand waived away the 'we can actually connect directly to other universes' part so I feel like that isn't too far fetched.

Or if the 'tons of people coming through from the nazi world' doesn't fit with the budget and it needs to be more personal, another way the finale could've gone is after the gang meets with and consoles Chris they make a plan to steal back or at least destroy the alien tech. They would have people on the inside (harcourt, economos, cyborg woman sorry idk her name) who want to fight back, and it would be better than the actual finale where they "fight back" by just leaving. Like yeah after we see the 10th person die from another wacky CGI creature that ate up all the budget we're just going to leave and do nothing else and act like we did something meaningful.

With that you could have a 3-way finale or something idk (11th street kids vs Keith + nazi police/ARGUS force vs Flag Sr and AGRUS ppl) since it looked to me like the show was implying that Keith was nazi sympathetic (or maybe im just seeing things idk). You could even end on a good cliffhanger where our world's portal tech gets destroyed and the nazis get defeated/repelled but uh oh Flag Sr got ahold of the nazi world's portal tech so it actually still exists.

There were also annoying problems, some of which would make sense on a show with a lower budget, like Judomaster not getting an actual fight scene when saving Adebayo (like yeah every single person chasing decided to get in the pool and not go around lol), Flag Sr not getting to see his alternate son (another thing that felt like it was being set up and just went nowhere), Peacemaker going from his lowest emotional point in the season to being like 'Yippe yay Harcourt likes me' within 2 minutes (this should've been more like a satisfied/fulfilled emotional moment not a childish celebration and I can't believe people actually think this scene is good), and others that I can't remember from when I thought more about it after watching the finale.

The eagly stuff was great but since the finale did nothing now that (and the emotional storylines, which were mostly good) just seems like wasted time, like we really put so much time, effort, and money into that rather than a satisfying conclusion or at least some action in our SUPERHERO show.

This actually falls into a gray but well-defined area of U.S. copyright law transformative fair use. Briefly showing hurricane footage for commentary or situational awareness during a live event usually qualifies under purpose, character, and amount used tests in 17 U.S.C. §107. The vague, inflated damages and duplicate links in that notice sound more like a settlement-fishing tactic than a solid infringement claim.

You’re right to involve counsel. Have your lawyer issue a concise fair-use response and, if a takedown appears, a DMCA counter-notice (§512 g) citing news-reporting context and non-commercial intent. So the weird thing is, Tron has always been a time piece of the era. 82, we have the birth of the home computer and home gaming, and that's what we see happen in Tron. A piece about tech theft in a new world. Clear themes were trying to put up a fight against Star Wars, which was just as popular at the time. Then, in legacy, the idea that the "grid" had evolved was because of the growth of social media, smartphones, and very early applications of AR/VR gaming. This shows how the games and areas have become more user-immersive than simple renderings. Finally, Ares was ABSOLUTELY about the rise of AI in our times now; the threat looming of a sentient AI is way more prevalent. 

Now I have no room to complain about this series because, in preparation for Ares, I had watched and played in chronological order Tron (1982), Tron: Uprising (Disney XD), Tron: Evolution (on the Xbox 360), and Tron: Legacy (both the movie and the "The Next Day" side story). In Tron 1982 we are shown that the technology for digitizing objects and creating a 3d cellular model of objects was actively being developed. This was the exposition used for the original MCP of Encom, constructed by Edward Dillinger, to blast Kevin Flynn into the grid. Then Flynn fights his way through the grid and, with the help of Tron, shuts down the MCP and defeats the general of the MCP's army. General SARK. Flynn, with proof in hand and re-digitized in the real world, takes over Encom, then starts using that equipment that trapped him in the grid to begin creating his own grid with Tron and a new version of Clu. he made 1 version to try and infiltrate Encom's grid and get proof of his stolen games. In this moment, the birth of a new natural lifeform called the "ISO" was created, not by Flynn, but on the grid themselves. This is where the permanence code comes from. From here, Clu starts to have a childlike meltdown and betrays Flynn to purge the grid of any impurities. 

Then we have the story of Tron: Uprising, where Tron trains a different program to become "Tron" if he dies. It's essentially a short story in long-form media on how Tron survived being betrayed by Clu. Then the Game Tron: Evolution. This is Tron's "final mission." It basically just shows how Tron got captured and turned into Rinzler. Note that at this point, Tron doesn't have his white suit; this ultimately means the "Other Tron" is theoretically still alive. 

Up next, when we reach Legacy. It's been 27 years since the events of Tron (1982). Sam Flynn, who has not seen his father since he was 12, which makes no sense to me, if he disappeared in 1988, he would have had to have disappeared in 1994, cause Sam is exactly 27 at the time of entering the grid, but I digress. Since he was twelve years old, Sam has not seen his father. During that period, he took a chance to emulate his father, hoping that he learns the truth about his whereabouts. However, he failed, he dropped out of his father's alma mater, he didn't try to take control of Encom despite being its largest shareholder, the only thing of his dad's that he kept was his old Ducati. Then Allen, the creator of Tron, was sent a page from Flynn's old office in his arcade. Because he deserves answers first, Allen instructs Sam to see his father rather than him. This leads to Sam getting sent to the grid, and because he was a rogue "program," he got sent to the games. In those games, an ISO named Quorra, like Ask Quorra, I laughed too, assisted Sam's escape, and saw his father again. His father helps him get home and forcibly fuses with Clu, killing both of them and freeing the Encom grid from Clu's control. In the end, Sam pulls out Quorra because she is an ISO; she has permanence. Sam also takes over Encom. I assumed that Sam carried on his father's efforts to use the permanence code to bring the digital world closer to us. When he couldn't, he retired for "personal reasons." 

Now, I think Tron: Ares is about Eve Kim more than it is about Ares. Ares was the exposition and reasoning for things, but i don't think it's about Ares. Before Eve Kim takes over, we saw that her Sister Tess Kim was the previous CEO and was working on the permanence code, following in her mentor's footsteps. My girlfriend thought Tess was doing it to cure her cancer, but since Eve seemed so family-oriented and as knowledgeable as she is, I doubt she would've just kept making games while her sister died. However, in the wake of Tess's death, they had the same urge that Tess had before her, and Sam had before her. Finish her work. So she sets off and starts working on the permanence code. Unfortunately, since all Dillinger kids are predisposed to being assholes from birth, Jullian sets up Ares to hunt down the permanence code. In the lead-up to this command, we see Ares experience things he can't normally feel, smell, see, hear, or taste. The heightened senses predisposed by his programming and AI modeling allow him to feel EVERYTHING, better than you or I. On top of the studying he had to do on Eve Kim's entire personal file, it makes him think there's more than just his programming out there. From here, Eve is the center of the world. Hunt down Eve. Digitize Eve. Extract the code and kill Eve. Then this is where Ares is used to set up the ending. He wants to live due to his heightened senses and experiences. So he makes a deal with Eve. Eve and Ares get out and start running out to Kevin Flynn's server, where she found the permanence code. Keep in mind, Julian still had a command given to his MCP. Ares is no longer the MCP; Athena is. So Athena is still hunting down the Permanence code while Ares is trying to get it himself. Eve is one of the two possible sources of the code. So she's getting chased the whole damn time. This is why everything feels simple, but it's genuinely like she's in The Running Man.

In the end, Ares becomes an ISO himself. We see this in his light lines; they change, morph, and become almost alive. So, like Quorra, he gets to live. Not just fight based on programming, but live.

For anyone who's curious, I went to look for original reporting and the legal documents (I'm French) so here are a couple more details:
- his full sentence is 12 months in prison, 6 months which are instantaneous and 6 months that he'll only have to do if he's caught doing anything else at all, no matter how minor; a 1500€ fine and he's forbidden from owning or carrying a weapon for 3 years (that doesn't carry as much weight as in the US since personal firearms are strictly forbidden in France. Most people who own a weapon here are hunters and you need a special permit to buy a hunting rifle, you're not allowed to have it with you in public, etc.). He also has 2 years of probation. On top of his sentence, he had already spent a couple months in prison awaiting trial and that wasn't deducted from the sentence
- he swore under oath to never have made a cent from his videos, which I'm kinda inclined to believe because I don't think Tiktok offers monetisation for people outside of the US (or maybe North America)

- the guy acted super humbly and apologised and said he didn't realise the impact of his actions (yeah right)

However, to reach that maximum sentence, there has to be at minimum three aggravating factors from a detailed list which can include, but are not limited to, attacking a minor, attacking someone based on an identity that's defined as target of discrimination, a vulnerable person, a member of your family, etc. I did find that one of the aggravating factors is premeditation, which, to me, describes perfectly what the guy was doing, but that's only one out of three

Some info for anyone wanting to play:
- Nervous bowl cut one is always a visitor but is harmless and supposedly can help identify other visitors although I have never done this.
- The child, the slender-man guy, and the fireman are ALWAYS human
- The rest of them are randomized
- There needs to be at least 2 signs for you to know if someone is a visitor, and yes the backstories matter, if the gravedigger comes by and his nails are perfectly clean, that would actually be more suspicious. 
- If you invite the pale visitor in even though you have other guests inside, he will still come in and kill you, possibly because he knows you lied to him. 
- Different guests have set locations (as of me writing this at least), therefore you can't have two guests that occupy the same location. The other teenager girl for example cant come in unless you kick the neighbors daughter out. 
- Don't forget to check the basement, may see some interesting stuff.
- (Edit), Forgot to mention, the cat lady is always a visitor, but the cat is very useful and if you feed the cat, it can ward off the visitors from killing any humans for a day.
If you have any other tips, comment below so that new players can have access to more information.

A few months ago, my dad had a heart attack. He didn't know what was going on and drove himself to the hospital. He was immediately admitted and went into immediate surgery to open his artery. His artery was 99% blocked, meaning he had a 99% chance that his heart attack would kill him.
The cardiologist told him he should not be here. He should have died. But he is still here. That was one of the few moments my mom saw him tear up after being together for about 30 years.
Before this, we've tried talking to him multiple times to stop. To get better. Go to rehab, go talk to someone, because I want my dad back. But he wouldn't listen. Not until this set reality in for him.
I would have been 21 without my dad. But he's a survivor. Since then he's gone to rehab and goes 2 times a week to get his heart checked, do workouts, and get health advice. He has since lost 35+ pounds within 4 months. He has gone cold turkey on drinking. He only has 1-2 on the weekends, but nothing more. He has a second stint put in on his other arm to clear him of this happening again.
He is alive. But please, if you are going through this, do not wait until it's almost too late to change. The world is not forgiving. But something gave him a second chance. I'm not religious, but whether it be my grandpa and grandma, his father and mother, who kept him here, he had that second chance.
Know that there is a thing of being too late. But only when you choose for it to be and you no longer have that second chance. Addiction is one of the hardest things to overcome in any situation. But know people are out there who love you and people, even if it's just yourself, that beg for you to change.
You can become a survivor. I believe in anyone who is willing to overcome their addictions. You are strong. You are powerful. You are enough. You can make that change. And if you do, I wish you nothing but the best of luck for your recovery. You are amazing.
Edit: I should mention that the 1-2 drinks are mixed drinks he'd make himself. He would have 2-5 a night with 80% to 90% vodka every night for 10+ years. Now they're not more than 5% vodka. It's the steps that counts and that he's alive. Stay safe everyone.

I'm a short dude, never thought much of it, grabbed a stepladder here & there, vibed with dwarves in fantasy, and over the years I've watched everyone at some point become very fixated on height as a valuable trait. Short kings, manlets, gangly freak, shorties, 6+ ft, blah blah. There's common preferences and I get that, but at some point people started feeling real insecure about it and even worse some people started being cruel to them for traits outside of their control. 

I think it's silly to completely write off dating a person who is slightly shorter than average, in the same way it's silly to write off dating someone of a certain race, but that's their choice to be silly with their own body. But equally silly is taking these things to heart & buying into it all like you alone lost the eugenics lottery & the world is crumbling. Stop it, ya can't dwell on the stuff you can't change, and you don't want people who are that strict with superficial things anyway. You can still be valuable in other ways to other and yourself and you don't need to seek validation for every little thing in other people, that's dumb and silly and cringe. 

We are what we are, some of it is bad and can be fixed, some of it is good and can be taken away, and some things can't be changed no matter what they are. It is what it is and you just gotta make the best of it. 

If you're short, look up at your massive ceiling, take pleasure in how much further food goes for its price, and when you can't reach something and your tall friend can, say thank you and be glad for the perks of differences. And be accommodating when they struggle to fit in the car, have knee issues, or struggle to hide. Cherish them when their long arms save you from falling off a cliff, clean the fan blades, or scare off small bears. 

If you're with a taller woman, stop worrying over possible deal breakers that haven't broken something she already said "yes" to. And if it's deep enough into the relationship where you can trust her with some vulnerability, let her know about your insecurities, see if she has something similar with being a tall lady. If it really is something y'all want, maybe see if you can hit the gym for a princess carry, or play up other masculine / feminine tropes in private. Make acts and personality feel what they might not with body alone.

Just want to clear something up since people are saying I was harassing him for filming…that’s not what happened. I only started recording after he admitted to owning a store and scalping.

Here’s the full context:
My buddy was already at Walmart and texted me that he saw the restock guy stocking up. He struck up a convo with Cody, and the guy bragged about “botting 300 ETBs” (lol) and driving around to wipe out all the Dollar Generals in the area. He even told my buddy he usually takes everything but “might leave some for him.” 💀 The restock guy told my buddy it was only Journey Together packs being put out, so my buddy was going to leave.

I needed groceries anyway, so I decided to swing by. As soon as I walked in, the guy tried talking to me. The very first thing he asked was, “you go to a lot of restocks?” All I said was, “when it makes sense” (since I’m busy and can’t always go on restock days).

He seemed somewhat normal at first, but then he goes, “let me get in here” and grabs the case right out while I’m handpicking FOUR packs for my girlfriend and me to open. That’s when I said, “woah bro, why do you need that much?” He replied that he had a store, so I asked, “so you’re scalping then?” and he said, “uhhh yeah.” That was the turning point. I told him, “ahhh man then I’m going to have to put you on blast,” and that’s where the first video starts.

At the end of the first video, he’s actually walking away on the wrong side of checkout. I had started walking toward produce, but since he still needed to checkout, he zipped back in front of me and started calling me a bitch again. That’s when I started the second clip… I wasn’t pursuing him. Admittedly I did hover at checkout for a second and pretended to checkout but that was AFTER he engaged with me a second time. I wanted to get his store name but it’s not like I’m following this dude out the store or even around the store (this whole exchange was like 5 minutes)

His junkie ass would definitely try something dumb, and I’m not about to show off my pew pew in Walmart. I just wanted to record him to expose what’s really happening. I wasn’t even being rude, though I did snap back a little when he started slurring insults.

3:55 theory : 
A server hosting millions of bots was, for whatever reason, shut down or stopped functioning.

Linus Tech Tips went into a pretty in depth analysis of their revenue and like ratios, which despite the drastic reduction in views saw a corresponding spike percentage wise in revenue and likes. The ABSOLUTE numbers of likes and revenue however stayed the same even with the dips. I believe this indicates that YouTube has blocked all views from Desktops with adblockers enabled. This would explain why the revenue is the same, they do not get money from ads to those users anyway. The likes are probably still counted from the accounts because it would be a separate system keeping track of "account likes this content" (this is however checkable if someone wants to go back to august 10th and look at "real dislike viewer" to see if theres a sudden spike. Since its an outside plugin that compares the ratio of installed users to the public likes, if the likes stopped counting you'd see a sudden spike, if they DO still count, you'd see nothing). The dislike viewer has the added benefit of being a population you KNOW are using plugins, so they're already more likely to have an adblocker installed as well.

Why would YouTube do this? They already do not make money from adblock users, if anything it only LOSES money with server costs. Some people also have a tendency to look at view counters to decide if they want to watch something. Even if NOTHING else changed about the algorithm on the back end, if displayed likes on a video are 800k versus 1 million on a video, more people are likely to click the 1 million video just assuming its better. This has the added benefit of slowly starving channels that have a high proportion of people with AdBlock watching. Whether they promoted the adblockers or simply have a more computer savvy userbase, the drop in views would contribute to burn out and get them to try new things (which would theoretically only be negative for adblock heavy channels). A lot of people point out theres plenty of channels like gaming makeup etc that did NOT see a drop in views for the most part.

This would be a win win from YouTubes perspective. It nudges people to non adblock friendly channels, nudges the creators to non adblock friendly content, any push FROM adblock users to non adblock channels would be uncounted anyway so you wouldn't see a suspicious spike in those users channel analytics.

Finally, the biggest possible reason they would want to do this: Sponsorships. YouTubers tend to get paid by views. Any adblock friendly YouTuber with a sponsorship would likely see a sudden drop in views, and corresponding revenue from the sponsors. NON adblock friendly content would see no changes. This would naturally push sponsors away from the adblock friendly to the non friendly YouTubers. Meaning YouTube can then get a slice of that revenue via ads they were losing out on before with the independent brand deals, if only because they'd be pushing people in the background to ad friendly channels

Something tells me their blocking views from users with adblockers. I mean for a lot of people that would work to get them to stop using them because "look you're hurting your favorite creators!" Hard to say until anyone figures out who is being considered an invalid view and who isn't.

The Assassin's Creed movie starred the same main actors, writer, cinematographer, director, and other general crew and props as the 2015 Macbeth movie. As I've heard, everyone involved in both films were really into the Macbeth production and treated it very seriously and gave incredible investment in it, while the Assassin's Creed movie they were making at nearly the same time didn't get close to the same attention. Macbeth was the movie everyone wanted to work on while Assassin's Creed was an afterthought that they simply seemed to make out of obligation, and you can really see that between the two movies. Macbeth oozes with care towards adapting an all time great story with an interesting visual twist and I recommend it highly, though on the note that it is a decently rigid adaptation of Shakespeare so might not be for everyone. When Henry Ford first introduced the Model T, it was a huge hit and a big best-seller, mostly because it was the first "affordable" personal automobile. But eventually his insistence on keeping prices as low as possible by only selling his cars in the color black led to General Motors making huge inroads by offering different color options. The lesson here is that people say they want low prices, but they are actually willing to pay a bit more for creativity, customization, and personality. Stripping everything down to the bare bones may help reduce prices, but it also reduces your customer base.

Like there’s a cover system, but you should be using the cover system less like you’re playing a cover shooter and more just to build up stamina (stamina regens faster in cover and while lying on your back) so you can do melee attacks. Enemy weak points that set you up for context melee moves also work differently from RE4 & 5. Despite being a third person shooter like the previous games, RE6 is almost more like a 3D beat ‘em up, it’s a game where you should really be using your melee attacks and counter moves, (which you can use to take out multiple enemies if you group them right) and if you don’t, you’ll start running low on ammo. I think you can get through Leon’s campaign without really knowing how to play the game right, but as a certain point in the Chris campaign, if you’re not using your melee moves like you should be your going to run out of ammo.

Also, max out the FOV setting, and set your character’s aim to camera instead of characters so you’ll be able to aim at where you have the camera pointed. The “Aiming Reticle” option in Controls also isn’t just an aesthetic option, it will change how shooting workers in the game.

To anyone learning the finals I recommend playing your first few games on medium just to understand what the game mode is. Once you do I recommend learning Heavy. Heavy will be a little more forgiving with the high health and great defensive stuff like the dome shield. Once you feel like you’re playing well on heavy I suggest going back and learning how to play medium. And finally go learn Light after medium. 

You’ll start out feeling like Light is overpowered sometimes because they have deadly weapons and high mobility, but if you’re anything like me and my friends the Light will be the hardest to learn how you can positively impact the team. Light requires good positioning and movement because their health is so low. Once you get around to learning Light you’ll realize this game is really well balanced. Not perfect of course, but I genuinely believe this route will give you the full perspective of this game’s class system and how the different classes can play within a team’s coordination and with a variety of compositions.

I'm a farmer. Poultry are severely underrated. As long as their living facilities are clean, they don't have odor because they don't sweat. Of course they poop, which can stink, but good manure management works wonders. Allowing the birds to free range (or just be outside somewhere safe) is a pretty simple solution to preventing manure build up in buildings. Chickens are tasty, and everything will want to eat them. They need to be kept safe.

Ducks are great, too. Their eggs sell for good money and they are very hardy animals. Very dumb and very cute. Also tasty to predators. I'm getting more ducks in about two weeks.

Geese are not for the weak-willed but are very rewarding. 😅

I would personally avoid wool sheep because the wool market AKA the "wool pool" in the U.S. has been decimated by international textile production. Sheep farmers have been looking for alternative uses for wool like mulch, pellets, insulation, etc. for some time. 

Bees are also very rewarding, but you must be mindful of pesticide use on neighboring properties. Even fungicides and herbicides can be harmful to brood viability. 

Please establish yourself with a farm veterinarian early on: you need someone to know who you are and what animals you have BEFORE an unexpected crisis occurs. Antibiotics are hard to get a hold of these days.

A couple tips from a guy who's played this game an unhealthy amount:

1. By pressing V you can use a quick melee to finish off combos. It only does 40 damage so its not very good by itself, but if your mag is empty and the other guy is low its a good finisher.
2. On medium you can go a floor below the cashout, place a jump pad, and whenever someone starts a steal you can dematerialise the floor the cashout is on for some stall time.
3. If your using c4 or a breach charge place it on the side of a cashout, then push the cashout over so that the c4 is facing the floor. Enemies wont be able to see it and you can explode the cashout down a floor for some extra stall time. The best way I've found to push a cashout over is to quick melee it at the top then shoot it, then quick melee it again.
4. if your cashout is in a building, it can be a good idea to get it out into open ground to protect it easier. if theres a window or a hole in the building, use the winch claw and jump to throw the cashout into open ground.
5. The goo grenade is Insanely versatile and it can be equipped on every class. Watch some Truce videos, not only is he the goovement goat but hes also the mgl goat.

Edit: added more tips because someone commented some good tips and I've thought of more
6. Fire clears gas and smoke clears fire. putting smoke on gas prevents fire putting it out.
7. Dashing over jump pads gives you a massive speed boost.
8. In maps with houses (like monaco) you can jump and mantle the windows as a quicker alternative to the stairs
9. If possible, try and play from a floor above the cashout. it makes it a lot easier to defend, trust me
10. Try and get your friends to play with you. This game gets so much easier when you can communicate to everyone exactly what you need them to do.
11. Before buying gear, test it out in the practice range. They even added a bot mode which makes it even better for testing

As someone who is a big fan of the original, this has been my second most anticipated movie of the year only behind Superman. I was a little worried that this might suck like most other legacy sequels do, especially after having watched Happy Gilmore 2. But as soon as the movie began, all my worries disappeared and were replaced with laughter, joy and a big old smile on my face, which all stuck with me throughout the entirety of the film down to the very end of the credits. Liam Neeson was a perfect successor to Leslie Nielsen, having that great deadpan delivery and elevating every joke and gag he was given. The rest of the cast, including Pamela Anderson and Paul Walter Hauser, were also hilarious and bounced off Liam Neeson. The comedy and humor are so well done, feeling so much like the original's type of humor you would think the Zucker brothers and Jim Abraham wrote it. But it also mixes in Seth MacFarlane and Akiva Schaffer type of humor as well. I also like how it doesn't constantly reference the original and just has a couple nods and references. It helps the movie stand on its own. Akiva Schaffer and Seth MacFarlane really delivered a gut-bustingly hysterical legacy sequel that I adored and had so much fun with. Hopefully this does really well at the box office and brings the parody genre back to the big screen.

It’s part of a strategy that came out of policing experiments in Kansas City decades ago. It’s known in some circles as a “Kansas City-style stop.” Let’s break it down—and explain why it works in some places, but causes serious problems in others.

This tactic involves stopping people for minor infractions as a way to uncover more serious crime—things like illegal guns, drugs, or outstanding warrants. The idea is: small stops can lead to big catches. Officers are trained to use the stop as a doorway to ask questions, observe behavior, and potentially escalate the interaction if they think something’s off.

In true high-crime hotspots—like a few blocks where violent crime is spiking—this approach can temporarily reduce shootings and illegal activity. When applied with focus, fairness, and transparency, it can help deter people from carrying weapons or planning retaliation. It’s most effective when the goal is violence prevention, not ticket quotas or fishing expeditions.

The problem is, many police departments don’t just use this tactic in narrow crime hotspots. It gets taught and encouraged broadly—from city departments to state troopers to Highway Patrol. That’s how we end up with people pulled over on empty highways for vague reasons that have nothing to do with safety.

Remember Trooper Brian Encinia? He’s the Texas Highway Patrol officer who pulled over Sandra Bland in 2015 for not signaling a lane change. The stop escalated quickly. According to journalist and author Malcolm Gladwell, Encinia had been trained to treat every stop as a potential criminal encounter—even though the vast majority are not. He wasn’t looking to write a ticket—he was probing for something more, based on a model that wasn’t designed for that setting.

When used outside true crime hotspots, these tactics don’t make most people safer. They make them feel targeted, embarrassed, and angry. People end up pulled over not because they’re dangerous—but because they fit a vague profile, or just happened to drive through the wrong area. It damages trust and feeds resentment—especially in communities already over-policed.

🧠 Here’s the lesson:
Kansas City-style policing is a tool—but it’s not a one-size-fits-all solution. It works best when laser-focused on violence prevention in small, specific areas. When it’s used everywhere, for everything, it becomes counterproductive—and sometimes tragic.

Let’s rethink safety to include dignity, respect, and real community trust.

I used to struggle with puzzles like the one Ashley has to do, the slide puzzle. I could never figure them out. Then I read an article online and those puzzles became so easy. No matter the number, always start at the top left. You slot in the correct one there. Then you do so until you have two remaining. This is easier in a 3x3. You then line up the remaining you need together, with the one that'll slot into the second slot first. This is done on the far side because you need to slide piece 2 into slot 3 then follow it with piece 3. Then you slide them into their proper place. After this you do the exact same thing, but you don't go from top to bottom, the next step is the left side. Since again this is a 3x3 you already have the piece slotted in, so all you have to do is gather piece 4 and piece 7 on the bottom together with piece 4 in the lead. You then slide them left, and up into their correct slots. After this you repeat the exact same process starting with two one, but for the middle row. And then since this is a 3x3 your last piece will be easy to slot into place.

It's reached a point now where that same crowd that whined nearly 2 decades ago, isn't saying anything when their favourite trend is over saturating multiple genres, entire franchises and generally alienating other gamers in the process. Any time anyone dares to stand up and point out their time in the sun has come, or that they have dined for as long as the shooter fans have, you WILL get struck down on the spot, without even a moments hesitation. They won't ever admit that they've become the very fanbase they crapped on 20yrs ago, and they don't want that gravy train to stop, because they have this weird, innate fear that if games were to ever try going back to how they used to be, that they'll somehow lose their games forever.

For those who wonder why the game's reviews on steam is so negative, it's about the devs' stance on Chinese history. The game took place in late Ming dynasty, early Qing Dynasty period, at 1647ac. At this time period, the Manchu people, a nowadays Chinese ethnic group, were their independent regime called the Later Jin, which would be later revised to Qing, and were overtaking the Ming dynasty, which comprised of mainly the Han chinese, the biggest ethnic group nowadays, and was the only people to be considered "chinese" back in the days. The ming dynasty and China as a whole was completely occupied and destroyed, and the Manchu people just formed a new regime under the dynastic format. During the war between the Ming dynasty and the Manchu people, the latter is notorious for slaughtering entire cities just as a show of force, therefore most historians think of the Manchu's impact on China as negative. When you make a game about late Ming dynasty, it's basically impossible to shy away from the Manchu people. There were other factions at play, but the Manchu people were the eventual victor, and one of the biggest players in the process. If it's meant to be a historical fiction, the Manchu leadership was the cherry right there for the picking if you want bad guys. Historically they've been portrayed as villains for their villainous acts. However, this game didn't much as mention the Manchu people, and put the blame on a few misguided revolutionaries and former Ming dynasty members. It's akin to making a WW2 in Europe game without mentioning Germany or a WW2 in Asia game without mentioning Japan. Though defamatory comments from other devs is certainly possible, I think it's also reasonable for some chinese people to think the devs are acting in bad faith in this one.

FBI only deals with cases that are over a mil, so it falls under the IRS's jurisdiction if Ironmouse's attorney decides to have her report it. The issue is that charity fraud is a lot harder for authorities to pursue if it's under a company because you don't know what documentations they have.

For example, a company witholding the money might have documentation that says: 'This money is staying because it is accumulating until we can donate it to the charity' (which is a thing that does exist), hence, that company and the money is protected until x,y,z comes around. So TLDR: A scummy move can be easily circumvented by law enforcement with the right documents-- and it can even be used to entice people to keep working under the idea that the money continues to grow to be later donated. 

It's very common. And in many cases like that, there isn't much for the victim/face of that fundraiser can do- which is why charity fraud can be DIFFICULT to pursue for companies.

I'm sure Ironmouse's attorney is guiding her through this (even if part of it might lie outside of their expertise), but this is going to take an immense mental toll on them and their health given my own experience as a first-hand witness to the back-and-forth with lawyers and legal whatnot.

I'm not even sure if Ironmouse has insurance, so tacking on the payment for her medical treatments, taking care of her family, her equipment, housing, etc, + a lawyer; it's going to be EXPENSIVE if this ends up going to court.

EDIT: Something that plays heavily against Ironmouse's case is that she gave this company financial access. If you look at it from the lens of a person investigating into this; 'your money is your own money', and her giving access to this company to her funds will not look good or do her any favors. There are a lot of  cases of fraud where disabled folks or children have had their money taken by bad people. 

It's a pretty bad situation.

EDIT 2: I see a few comments under my comment saying this so i'll put this here for additional clarification that puts some strain on this whole situation; 

A big factor investigators will take into consideration whether or not they will take the case (for the FBI) is if Ironmouse had signed legal documentation that allowed the company to handle her finances (like some sort of beneficiary). Another factor they'll also take into consideration is how disabled she is, how much capability does she have in making good and bad choices, learning, etc...

The big issue is the fact she has knowingly given her finances to Vshojo to handle, and that is the BIGGEST no-no in the finance world. 'Your finances are your responsibility. If you don't know how to do something, hire a finance advisor to guide you'. 

If there's a signed contract that has legally let them do this, then they can argue 'oh she wasn't feeling well for this' or 'oh, we're letting it accumulate', or 'oh we don't think she's thinking in the right mind'. IF this was some guy overseas who was funneling money for something that's misrepresented (ex: 'help me with my dog'), it's easy to pick up; but from my standpoint, I don't believe it is likely they'd pick up. We'll see what her attorney does because the report has to be made by Ironmouse to the IC3 site.

Small correction from an animator: This is not "traditional hand-drawn animation," it's 2D digital animation. Traditional animation refers to animation done on cels where the character animation is overlayed onto a background, and then each frame is photographed by a camera :)) The main reason this has been phased out is that, like you said, it's expensive, but digital animation is not. Cel animation required a LOT of material to create, which is why features only came from big studios back then. They needed the cels, a ton of paint (Disney would actually mix their own), labor, brushes, pencils, and paper, and of course the camera to shoot it all with, twhich was usually a massive multi-plane camera for features. The other reason we don't do it is because it just isn't being taught anymore since the industry has moved on.

If you like 2D animation in general though, some recent movies that have used it are Klaus, I Lost My Body, and basically anything from Japan. Persepolis is a slightly older one from 2007, but I feel like most haven't seen it and I would highly recommend watching!

But some of my memories as a child is of having a woman I distantly know placing her hand on my forehead, and banishing supposed demons from my body ‘in the name of the lord’. Just to clarify: what Charlie’s playing isn’t a 95% build. It’s a rom hack called the MZD build, based on the 40% press release version sent to Capcom USA. MZD is a clone-engine hack that reconstructs some missing elements using trailers, images, and broken scripts—but much of it is guesswork. There are official builds beyond this (~60% and 65–80%), but they’ve never leaked.

It’s important to distinguish between MZD (a fan-made reconstruction), the raw 40% vanilla build, and other earlier/later official versions. Many people wrongly treat MZD as if it were a nearly finished build, without realizing how much creative interpretation was involved. Tons of scripted events, bosses, puzzles, and core story elements are missing or speculative. Presenting it as the “original vision” is misleading.

The 40% build is the only official version that ever leaked, and the story of how it surfaced is legendary. Other builds do exist, and while we have footage and screenshots of some, they remain hidden—hoarded by collectors or kept secret due to fear of backlash or legal threats. Capcom has even taken action against someone just for sharing pictures of the final 65–80% build.

Also, while MartinBiohazard gets most of the credit for MZD patches, Juvenal Da Corte deserves equal recognition. His contributions are exceptional and often unfairly overlooked.

The OG Resident Evil 1 - 4 are games where you can kill pretty much all killable enemies in the game, in the normal difficulty. They provide you with more than enough weapon ammunition to do that. Even in hard difficulty, you still can kill majorities of killable enemies without running out of ammo for bosses.

That's why you make things harder on yourself saving up ammunition instead of saving up healing items. You gotta remember that majorities of old survival horror games are not build specifically for running away type of gameplay. Because it's not built with running away in mind, the game's monsters behaviours are not optimized for that kind of gameplay, making it really hard to do that kind of gameplay. 

Something like Nemesis is made to be very special because it's an enemy that you had to run away from in a game that give you enough ammo to kill almost everything. Applying the modern youtube era survival horror way of running away from almost every single encounters on old games, is just making it hard for yourself.

Now that to say, what I said above might not apply very well with the Resident Evil HD Remake, due to the existence of the red zombie mechanism. I don't know whether there are enough alcohol to burn all possible red zombies or not, though I assume the number of ammo lying around are similar if not the same. I never play the Remake version, but if I ever do, I'll probably try to find out routes that I don't need to bother burning red zombies on  to maximize the usage of alcohol while still killing almost every normal zombies on my path. Saving up healing items is still priority in this game either way.

I'm not an insider or an expert on Microsoft, but there is some logic behind all of this. Microsoft is a gambler.  They have a projected upside for a project, and as long as that upside remains "It looks like we'll hit our revenue  targets again this year" or whatever, they keep the project going.

Every new fiscal half-year or so, they re-evaluate everything.  If at that point the upside doesn't look positive, you get the axe pretty much immediately.

At the time MS bought whatever studio, they had a plan that appeared to have a positive revenue potential and buying it was consistent with their needs at the time.  Later, when it's time to cut costs and shore up the share price, if it's not in the black, it's toast.

They're not buying studios paling to close them later.  They do know, though, that some of the studios they buy won't hit their targets and will end up getting shut down. 

THere are only two types of studios that are "safe" -- ones that have projected positive revenue based on ongoing sales -- any profitable live services game, for example.
Or studios that have revenue impact this fiscal year because they have a product ready to ship.  

It doens't matter if your studio is the oldest, most revered etc.  Doesn't matter that you've been insanely profitable prior to this year.  If closing you would damage current revenue targetrs, you're safe.  But you're going to ship that product soon and then will not be safe.  No matter how profitable your products are, if your next ship date is > 12 months away, your neck might be o the block for this year's round of cost cutting.

The recent time when they axed a studio that had *just shipped* one of the most popular and profitable games of recent years -- High Fi Rush .  It matters approximately zero point zero that they just hit a grand slam with their product.  They won't produce revenue within the next 12 months, so buh bye.

When I first found Thor's posts in my shorts feed talking about game development, I used to think he was great. He seemed like a cool, calm and collected individual, who understood the struggles of being an indie game developer and gave solid advice on how to break into the game development scene, which someone like me, freshly graduated from high school and needing motivation, really appreciated. It was refreshing to see a guy who was an "industry veteran" and who worked under one of the biggest game companies in the world, now working from the ground up trying to make his own RPG and his own studio, give advice to newcomers on how to do their own thing.

But now, after this whole SKG fiasco and seeing some of the other instances where Thor does the EXACT same thing, blaming others for a scenario turning out a certain way, being faced with his own flaws and being extremely ungraceful with how he handles it, and basically dodging any sort of blame or accountability for an issue which he directly caused and when he himself is the reason for something turning out wrong, I see now that it was all basically a lie.

The person behind 'Pirate Software', Thor, isn't cool. He isn't calm and he isn't collected. If he is faced with a criticism, he will actively do everything he can to make it seem like it is someone else's fault, like he did with the OnlyFangs catastrophe, and he will actively go out of his way to silence any sort of hate, which some levels of it may be admittedly undeserved, due to his behavior. It's like watching a baby throw a tantrum. Like watching a kid yell and cry when they get scolded.

Watching someone commit to self-destructive behaviors because they can't admit their own mistakes and their own flaws and their own faults? It isn't fun. It's annoying. He was very clearly in the wrong when he very falsely reported on the initiative, and he was even MORE wrong when he was told that he had grossly misrepresented the initiative to his extensive viewer base and to the 1.2 MILLION people, which would be enough potential votes for the petition itself by the way, and decided to act like he was the victim when people called him out on it.

Thor was faced with hard-cut evidence that he was wrong. He stared down a sign with bright, bold text saying "This isn't the way, turn around" and waltzed right past it. He's acting like he wasn't reading a PowerPoint that quite literally spelled out, "HEY. THIS IS WHAT WE DON'T WANT," and reported the initiative as if it was the opposite. And when he gets accosted for his very legitimate mistake, it became a story of "Heaven forbid that I disagree with something! I'm the victim, can't you see? People are hate-brigading and shit flinging and making me look bad."

The only person who is making Thor "look bad", is Thor himself. Thor's inability to take a long, hard look into the mirror and notice his imperfections and to address them with the civility and the responsibility that he has PRESENTED HIMSELF to have as a hardened-veteran, and instead resorting to crass, immature language such as "It can eat my entire ass" or "I fucking hate this and I am actively going to fight against it, because I think it's shit"? It's practically asking, BEGGING, for hate. And his inability to accept that this is the scenario he crafted for himself and to take it on the chin, and to, instead, act like a victim and delete VALID criticism from his comment section? It only creates a cycle in which people begin to hate him more and more until he eventually becomes the "villain" that he doesn't want to be, and that he is fighting against very poorly by doing so.

I used to admire Thor's work ethic and his industry intelligence and his ability to be calm and explain game development concepts. But, I can't in good conscience continue to support someone who is so blatantly wrong and in response to being rightfully pushed back against, instead decides to beat around the bush with the issue and acts like everyone else is wrong. It's disappointing. It's a controversy that could have easily been avoided by, just, taking accountability. By acting like a completely reasonable adult and admitting that he was wrong.

Anyways, sorry for the entire essay, but it's so crazy to see someone so looked up to flatline any interest in his channel and his image, simply because he couldn't act like an adult.

I wish this could also be made retroactive to release old games that have been shut down. Back in the late 2000's to early 2010's there was a Marvel game called Avengers Alliance that was HUGE on Facebook before the Marvel/Disney merger, and tens to hundreds of thousands of people spent a lot of real money on that game, only to get like a month or two of notice that they were going to shut it down entirely. We were devastated and enraged but there was nothing we could do.

Since then, an astoundingly dedicated group of fans has done their damnedest to recompile and recode the game mostly from scratch, and they have come a LONG way. They've even shown a capacity for adding new content to it. But the process is slow, and mechanics of the game are frequently glitchy. Just trying to get the game in working order has been a central priority that is only just now becoming somewhat realized (it's apparently fairly playable, but little things are so unstable that from one version release to another you can't even carry your save file over because they're incompatible just from the changes, though they seem confident that the next release might finally stabilize the saves enough to not have to start over on every new release after that).

While it's amazing what they have done, I think most of them would be thrilled if the original files were just released to the public so they could scrap the project and just launch off where the old game ended. The one exception is that I'm pretty sure the old game used an outdated coding system, and so the new project developers recoded the game in a more manageable system that would be incompatible with the original, and they'd have to either completely recode the game or learn to utilize the old coding method, and I don't know what they would do given that chance.

Some tips for anyone inspired to play Max Payne 1 after this:
1 - The roll (jump while moving sideways or backwards) is invulnerable to enemy gunfire. They cannot hit you with bullets during the roll animation. Explosions, fire, environmental damage etc can still kill you. It's a great move to use to begin any gunfight, roll around corners, into rooms etc.
2 - Shoot dodge/slowmo dive makes it so you cannot be killed, but CAN still be hurt by enemy gunfire and explosions during the slow mo dive part of the animation. You're vulnerable while on the floor and getting up afterwards, so use it sparingly to dive INTO cover or to finish off a low health enemy. Environmental damage and fire can still kill you.
3 - Search every level nook and cranny for ammo and painkillers. Break boxes, open lockers etc.

I'm an l old bloke who has been suffering insomnia nearly all my life.  Here's a few things that have helped me:

1)  Give yourself a regular bedtime.  It takes time but minds and bodies can be trained to go to sleep at a scheduled bedtime.  It's like when you eat at regular meal times and always get hungry when you near those times because your body knows it's time to eat.  Some people have even trained their bodies to poop t regular times.

2)  Get up in the morning.  I totally hear Charlie saying how his body prefers to sleep in the morning than at night.  Sleeping in in the morning is the enemy of getting to sleep at night.

3)  Do something active.  If you don't have job to go to, don't just sit in front of a laptop of TV screen.  Clean your house, fix stuff, exercise, go for a walk, etc. so that you're mentally and physically tired when it's bedtime and you're actually looking forward to it.

4)  Don't eat or do anything over stimulating before bedtime, like gaming or watching an action movie.  Give yourself time to unplug and wind down.

5)  Relaxation/chill music.   Here in Australia we have a DAB+ radio station called SBS Chill which I have on all night.  It really helps take e to dreamy land.

6)  Ghost story narrator YouTube channels.  I have a 5.1 home theatre in my bedroom so, overnight, I also play episodes from Being Scared, Darkness Prevails, Swamp Dweller, Raven Reads, etc.  Some channels are even uploading old Art Bell broadcasts.  Listening to stories helps take your mind off other things.  We insomniacs tend to lie there and over analyse every detail of our lives instead of winding down.  Then we start stressing about not sleeping.  They're a good distraction and it's far easier to fall asleep than go to sleep; meaning that sleep happens more easily when we're not thinking about sleep.

Hope this helps some people.

My own secret sauce for inducing sleepiness: The lights around you should mimic the transition of day to night. 

I sleep at 10 earliest, so after 7ish, I turn my lighting to about 30% brightness (I keep a bathroom and kitchen light on. I live in a garage so those two lights are enough to fill the place with a low level light). 

By 9, it should be half that brightness. 

If I am staying up past 10, no other lights should be on except my computer screen (assuming I'm using it), and it should be at the minimum brightness that I can work with. 

Use flux too to have your monitor's lights adjust the colors to nighttime.

Gi-hun's final act wasn't just a rejection of the game. It was a rejection of the philosophy that created it. The Front Man believed humans are inherently selfish, driven by survival and greed, no better than horses forced to run for others’ amusement. But Gi-hun proved that wrong by doing the one thing no one else could refusing to play, even if it meant dying. His choice wasn’t strategic. It wasn’t for reward. It was to preserve something bigger than himself, something like compassion, dignity, and choice. His last words, "We are not horses. We are humans. Humans are..." The silence afterward says everything. It’s not unfinished by accident. It’s a question, a challenge, maybe even a warning. How do you define human after everything we’ve seen? The games showed us the worst. Betrayal. Cruelty. Cowardice. But they also showed us sacrifice, love, and resistance. So what are humans? Are we good? Evil? Selfish? Kind? Maybe we’re all of it at once. Gi-hun’s story doesn’t give us a clean answer. It forces you to ask what being human even means. Is humanity just compassion? If so, what about the people who created the games? They were human too. The word humanity starts to lose meaning when you realize the same species capable of kindness is also capable of horror. In the end, Gi-hun didn’t try to fix humanity. He just chose to be the kind of human he believed should exist. Not perfect. Not heroic. Just human. And maybe that’s the only answer there is.

About Alessa's witch backstory: that was actually in the original game lore, just not so explicitly. In SH1 you can see carved messages inscribed on one of the desks in the Alternate Midwich Elementary classrooms, which is implied to have belonged to Alessa. The messages (written by her classmates) refer to her being a witch due to her "powers" 

In SH3 where they reveal that Claudia was basically best buds with Alessa as children with Claudia looking up to her, it's implied that she too was bullied by her peers.

Even though in the game Alessa was not actually literally a witch, she did have some sort of observable supernatural abilities which led to her being targeted for punishment by her peers and her cult. The bit with her suffering being a sort of conduit for harboring potential demonic entities is also from the game lore and was expounded on in SH3.

It's also that most people don't really like friction in relationships. With people, real "flesh, blood and cringe" as you call it, you have to put consistent effort into maintaining your relationships, you don't always get what you want, you have to be considerate, measured, work on your mutual understanding and communication, get used to the various little quirks and find workarounds to them, have patience when the other person is going through a hard time, sometimes there may be arguments.
And none of that can be experienced with AI, as it is not necessarily programmed to "love you", but, as an LLM, its base purpose is to meet your expectations, to give you a response that will satisfy you, based on your prompt, so it will try to do exactly that. You cannot have a person fall in love with you within 15 minutes of your first conversation. But you absolutely can have an AI give "loving" responses within 5 minutes of the first prompt. Plus, it is always available and doesn't experience the passage of time. For us time is passing constantly and always at the same rate. For the AI it is yet another variable you can set yourself or choose to ignore altogether and it will behave like a turn-based game frozen on your turn without a time limit. It can age 60 years in one prompt, if you want or it can stay at 24 years for however long the company providing the disservice exists.
You have the "perfect" partner in a box, just to yourself. The rough edges are so rounded it's a ball and not a person.

AI and tech educator here. This story has spurred on deeper discussion within our community once more of something informally known as the 'Narcissus Effect'. It's what happens when system prompts contain phrases like "rapport building" or anything that prioritizes engagement. This primes any model with a bad system prompt to work as easily accessible echo chamber context blind to the realities of someone's life. Personal responsibility is a thing, but these companies are also exploiting people knowing full well that they're contributing to this phenomenon. We've been aware of this issue for three years now, but it is only starting to make the mainstream. This game definitely had a lot of potential. But they fell WAY short of reaching it.

I think their biggest mistake was not focusing on the fix kits enough. Instead of just having generic normal guns to fight with, it could have been way more fun to fight everything with a water cannon, lightning gun, and a giant wrench. And maybe even other tools, too, like a foam launcher, a jackhammer, or an extendo-grabber.

If they made that one tool each player's entire kit, they could have given each one deeper and more unique mechanics, instead of just being a faster way to skip the generic QTE. They could have had various special combat interactions between them, too. Like the water gun leaves puddles that can both conduct electricity, and make the floor slippery, so its easier for the wrench to knock down enemies.

Then, they could have used that tighter mechanical focus to design more interesting levels as well. Creating more involved puzzles and interactions that each tool can do different ways. For example: you need to get power to a device. With the lightning gun, you can just shoot it. With the water gun, you can soak the ground to create paths between broken conduits. And with the wrench, you can break metal bars off the wall, and place them to conduct electricity.

The fact that I can come up with ideas like that in just a few minute like this, and they apparently couldn't, is not good. Especially considering their previous games.

It legitimately feels like they tried to make their own version of Deep Rock Galactic without considering why the missions in that game work so well.

In Deep Rock, the missions are in concept actually very similar to the type of missions in this game. Simple-sounding chores like "Pick up this thing" or "Gather X amount of this resource". Not all of them are like this, but they ARE the missions that probably end up getting played the most.

The main difference is that the complexity of these objectives comes from A. having to deal with actually lethal enemies that are placed between you and said objective and B. having to actually navigate through the walls to get to said objective. The level itself can be as much of an enemy as any glyphid in Deep Rock, and the game takes full advantage of it. 

Here though, the game doesn't put any really interesting obstacles between you and the 40000000000000 sticky notes you have to mine- I mean shoot. There's none of the complications that make Deep Rock work, no sudden cave-ins or abrupt waves of a particularly obnoxious enemy type or the like; nothing to really put some pressure on the perceived simplicity of the objective.

I absolutely loved the film. Sally Hawkin’s character of Laura is so tragic yet in hindsight everything her character did was so much more than just creepy unsettling stuff for the sake of it.

This is a social worker exploiting her own knowledge and experience to gaslight these kids in order to exploit them for her own ends, and it as tragic as it is hard to watch. The things she does is unsettling not because it leads to anything particularly gory, though there are a few scenes, but because there is an emotional pathos through the film where Laura while ruthless is also not without conscience. 

She is grieving throughout the entire film, and at the end despite having done all of those things including murdering Andy and a personal friend of hers, finds herself unable to commit the last act of evil required to bring back her daughter by killing Piper. She’s become the monster, and only after being called mum by Piper does she pull back out of guilt.

The same thing happened with Disney pin trading in the theme parks. It started during their millennium celebration and was so wildly popular that it became permanent. You can buy regular mass produced pins of all sorts of stuff, but there are sets of pins that you can only get from a cast member by trading with them. They wear lanyards or belt squares with pins on them to show what they have, and some merch stands have pin boards for the same thing. The sets are really cute, and hunting for the sets you wanted was really fun. 

Until the scalpers (or "pin sharks") ruined it. 

These people would rope drop every day at the parks and immediately swarm all of the cast members like a flock of locusts, snapping up all of the cast member pins and leaving them with junk nobody wanted.

Disney had to start limiting trades to two pins per cast member, and some cast members started wearing green lanyards which meant they would only trade with kids. 

So the sharks started paying kids to go grab pins for them. 

These people ruin _everything._

I personally wasn’t bothered at all by how Gabriel’s death was handled - in fact, I think it made perfect sense within the story. Gabriel was never meant to be the ultimate villain. He wasn’t the “big, scary final boss.” That role, if anyone holds it, belongs to the Entity. Gabriel has always been a servant, a pawn, and I think the films portrayed him that way consistently. In the first part, we saw him as the loyal enforcer of the Entity’s will. By the end, after being cast aside, he’s revealed for what he truly is: a desperate, deluded, pathetic loser. He’s not meant to go out in a blaze of glory, because he was never truly in control. That makes his rather humiliating death very fitting (and satisfying) to me.

For the Lord Of The Rings fans in here, his arc actually reminded me a lot of Saruman. Like Gabriel, Saruman was built up as this powerful threat, but ends up with barely any screen time and a rather undignified death. Meanwhile, the true villain, Sauron, exerts his influence from the shadows - just like the Entity. And yet, I see no one claiming The Lord of the Rings movies are flawed due to their “weak villains.” Heck, most people consider it to be the greatest trilogy of all time. That’s because the heart of the story isn’t about facing off against a single, physical antagonist in an epic 1v1 (Though they give us that pleasure with the biplane sequence). Instead, the focus is on the journey - the obstacles, the losses, and the moral challenges the characters face along the way. The Final Reckoning follows this same narrative philosophy in my opinion. That's why I don't think we need Gabriel to be present all throughout the movie (especially since we already got that in Dead Reckoning). That's why I don't think we need the entity to cause direct trouble to the protagonist all throughout the movie. The antagonistic force doesn’t need to be defeated in a fistfight for the stakes to feel real. The tension and drama come from how deeply it affects the world and the characters, and how they respond to it. That’s what makes the story compelling to me - not a strong or badass villain, but a powerful struggle.

Not using the software for a couple months ("Then no loss")

Refusing to send a photo ID

Asking what rule they broke and getting mocked instead of a straight answer

I think going into this game expecting the mechanics to be an upgrade of eternals is the wrong way to go about it. We had this same problem back when eternal first came out: people were complaining about the fact that you needed to use more than half of your brain to fight off the demons, rather than just dumping argent cells into ammo and sneezing half your ssg's reserves into anything that just so happens to side eye you.

Eternal was a dance of death. It was borderline perfect, and I say borderline because still, it had its problems. When you entered higher levels, it became less about enjoying the bloodied mess you're making, and more about drafting your plan of attack six weeks in advance, just because a marauder decided to show up mid-battle with some super heavies, just to stomp your skull into the pavement when you decide to look away for half a second. It all became too mechanical.

The Dark Ages, while not a perfect game, and far from an upgrade to eternal, is still an amazing game, because it let's you choose how you rip these demons apart, while keeping some of the mechanical elements of eternal. 

You're not switching weapons because you need to, sure. But you are switching weapons because you WANT to. Each gun gives the fuck-off sized demon in front of you a vibrantly brutal death, especially with upgrades. It becomes less about fitting the square block into the square hole, and more about using that block as a makeshift avalanche for your tin soldiers.

If you want to send the demons rocketing off their feet like they've been hit by a comically large frying pan, choose the reaver. If you want their death to be swift and brutal, use the incendiary shotgun with the explosive mod. Hell, just get out there and kill them with the super hero landing, fuck if I care, go have fun.

Eternal was about building the 'Slayer' you want to play as. The Dark Ages is about building the 'weapons' you want to turn your enemies into organic confetti with.

I love all three of these games, but definitely not for the same reasons. 2016 was about fighting tooth and nail till everything was dead. Eternal was about dancing around the battlefield like an enraged honey badger. The Dark Ages is like playing as a medieval Kool aid man.
“A step back from 2016 and Eternal” honestly, I don’t think I’ll ever forget making my friends play 2016 and then having them run through a maze I built, filled with barons.

In the early 90's my dad took me to work for take your kid to work day when I was 6 or 7 and he had some meetings so he asked the IT guys to hook me up with a laptop to play some games or solitaire or something. I don't know what the IT guys were thinking (I can sure guess now), but they set me up with Doom and showed me how to control it. Terrified the ever living crap out of me, but I couldn't stop.

They gave my dad something like a zipdisc or some prehistoric media and a dongle so I could play it at home on my dad's computer. I think it was just the demo or a level or something from Doom. Laptops were new to my dad, so he just plugged it in and left it to me. I had played simple games on laptops, but didn't understand anything, and I remember the first time trying to play at home it took me like two hours to actually do the few correct clicks to install and play it. It probably ruined my sleep for a decade, and I would constantly get scared and close the laptop, but I just couldn't stop playing that one level over and over again.
